name: Eliel
overview: Eliel was a male member of the tribe of Gad, noted in Scripture as the seventh Gadite to join David. He came to David at Ziklag, demonstrating his allegiance during a critical period of David's leadership. His role reflects the support David received from various tribal leaders.
namesAndTitles: The name Eliel means 'G-d is my G-d,' indicating a personal recognition of God. This proper name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 12:11 and does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries significant spiritual meaning.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Eliel as a descendant of Gad, linking him to the tribe of Gad. Beyond this tribal association, no other family relationships are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Eliel's significance lies in his position as a supporter of David during his early reign, particularly as the seventh Gadite to come to David at Ziklag. This highlights the gathering of tribal leaders who recognized David's future as king and contributed to the unity of Israel under his leadership. His inclusion in the list of David's followers underscores the tribal support essential for David's consolidation of power.
